146 (0.7 apg) }} '''Vakeaton Quamar "Von" Wafer''' (born July 21, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. Wafer has previously played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Houston Rockets]], [[Boston Celtics]] and [[Orlando Magic]]. He was the 39th overall selection (ninth pick of the second round) in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the Lakers. His nickname is "The Dutch Cookie".{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?id=5403986|title=Cookie Rojas among Page 2's All-Dessert team|date=2010-07-24|work=ESPN|access-date=2010-08-23}} ==High school== Wafer attended Pineview High School in [[Lisbon, Louisiana]] during his freshman, sophomore and junior years of high school. He averaged 32 points, 10 rebounds and 7 assists during his junior season. Up to that point, Wafer was a virtual unknown on the national recruiting scene. Tim Loring, the coach of the Arkansas Wings [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, invited Wafer to play for them the summer before his senior year. This allowed Wafer to display his skills on a wider stage, and by the end of the summer, he was considered to be one of the top ten seniors on many recruiting lists. He was also briefly at [[R.L. Paschal High School]] and [[Laurinburg Institute]] his senior year before deciding to attend and play at Heritage Christian Academy in [[Cleveland, Texas]], where he averaged 26 points, 8 rebounds, 4 steals, and 4 blocks per game. Wafer was the seventh [[McDonald's High School All-American]] to play at [[Florida State University]]. During the game, he scored 8 points and finished second to [[LeBron James]] in the McDonald's All-American slam-dunk contest.{{cite news|url=https://www.sptimes.com/2003/11/19/Sports/Buzz_grows_over_renew.shtml|title=Buzz grows over renewed 'Noles|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=2003-11-19|work=St. Petersburg Times|access-date=2009-04-08|archive-date=December 4, 2003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031204021258/https://www.sptimes.com/2003/11/19/Sports/Buzz_grows_over_renew.shtml|url-status=bot: unknown}} ==College== During his freshman year at [[Florida State University]] in the 2003–04 season, Wafer averaged 7.9 points in 17.5 minutes a game with the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Seminoles]]. He ranked third among all [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] freshmen with 43 three-point field goals made and scored in double figures 12 times. As a sophomore during the 2004–05 season, he led the team in scoring (12.5 ppg) and three-point field goals made (65). He made more than one three-point field goal in 14 games and surpassed the 20-point mark on six occasions. Despite some success that year, he was suspended for two games early in the season and benched frequently later. The ''[[Tallahassee Democrat]]'' reported that his family explained the suspensions were because of missed classes and study sessions.[http://www.tallahassee.com/mld/tallahassee/sports/11993658.htm ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070402095700/http://www.tallahassee.com/mld/tallahassee/sports/11993658.htm |date=April 2, 2007 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/video/channels/top_plays/2008/12/10/nba_20081209_botn.nba/index.html?player=top_plays |title=Block of the Night – NBA Videos and Highlights |work=NBA.com |date=2008-12-10 |access-date=2010-12-29}} ==Professional career== Wafer declared himself as an early-entry candidate for the [[2005 NBA draft]] after his sophomore year at FSU despite many draft experts predicting he would not be drafted. There were several hurdles he had to overcome to become a viable option for an NBA team to select him. Wafer was not invited to the annual [[Chicago]] pre-draft camp, which provides players who are not viewed as first-round prospects a chance to display their abilities in front of NBA team personnel. During a workout with the [[Phoenix Suns]], Wafer reportedly was frustrated by the physical play from [[Jan Jagla]], and responded by laying an intentional elbow to Jagla's nose, then walked off the court and ended the workout at that point.{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/d05/tracker/player?playerId=18821 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710084251/http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/d05/tracker/player?playerId=18821 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 10, 2012 |title=Von Wafer Draft Bio |publisher=ESPN.com Insider |access-date=2010-12-29}}{{cite web |url=http://www.hoopshype.com/articles/predraft_rodecker.htm |title=Articles – The final recap |publisher=HoopsHype |date=2005-06-13 |access-date=2010-12-29 |archive-date=June 18, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050618022343/http://hoopshype.com/articles/predraft_rodecker.htm |url-status=dead }} Los Angeles Lakers scout Irving Thomas, who played two seasons at FSU, saw three Seminoles games during the 2004–05 season and helped arrange a workout for Wafer with the Lakers.[http://www.tallahassee.com/mld/tallahassee/sports/colleges/florida_state_university/12019110.htm ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070402095525/http://www.tallahassee.com/mld/tallahassee/sports/colleges/florida_state_university/12019110.htm |date=April 2, 2007 }} Lakers general manager [[Mitch Kupchak]] saw enough of Wafer's ability that they used the second of their two second-round picks to select Wafer in the draft. Wafer was placed on waivers by the Lakers on October 26, 2006. He played in only one pre-season game due to a bruised left heel.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/0607_waivers.html |title=LAKERS: 2006–07 Waivers |work=NBA.com |date=2006-10-31 |access-date=2010-12-29}} Wafer then played for the [[Texas Legends|Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] during 2006–07, and was named Player of the Month in January 2007.[http://oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=3422314 Colorado Guard Von Wafer D-League Player of Month], February 2, 2007 He was signed to a ten-day contract by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on February 21.[http://www.insidehoops.com/wafer-clippers-022107.shtml Clippers sign Von Wafer] He played one minute{{Cite web |url=http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nba/article/0,2777,DRMN_23922_5482656,00.html |title=Nuggets add two guards |access-date=2007-04-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930222000/http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nba/article/0,2777,DRMN_23922_5482656,00.html |archive-date=2007-09-30 |url-status=dead }} without scoring before being waived a week later.[http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/conroy_10day_070228.html Clippers Sign Will Conroy to 10-Day Contract] On April 12, 2007, the [[Denver Nuggets]] signed Wafer for the remainder of the 2006–07 season. On February 21, 2008, the Denver Nuggets traded Wafer to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Taurean Green]]. Wafer changed his number from 22 (which he wore with the Nuggets) to 24, as number 22 had been [[retired number|retired]] by the Trail Blazers to honor [[Clyde Drexler]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/f-258910-1218.html |title=Trail Blazers acquire Von Wafer from Denver in exchange for Taurean Green |access-date=2008-02-21 |work=nba.com }} ===Houston Rockets=== Wafer was signed by the Houston Rockets and managed to keep a spot on the team due to his hot shooting in the preseason. On January 13, 2009, Wafer scored a career-high 23 points on 10–14 shooting in 39 minutes against the Los Angeles Lakers. He found a regular place in the Rockets' starting lineup due to good performance as well as an injury to regular starter Tracy McGrady. He continued to impress by scoring 21 points versus the Jazz and hitting the game-winning three at a game in Boston that the Rockets won 89–85. In that month he averaged 14.3 points per game. After Wafer moved to a team in Greece, the Rockets offered him a contract midway through the next season. He signed the contract, but failed his physical, so he could not join the Rockets. ===Olympiacos Piraeus=== Wafer joined the [[Greece|Greek]] [[Euroleague]] club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]] in August 2009, signing a two-year $10 million [[gross income]] contract.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4394104 ESPN.com Wafer says he's signed with Olympiakos.][http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/6569733.html Chron.com Wafer takes game overseas Ex-Rockets G gets big pay raise from Olympiakos; former team seals deal with Andersen.] He was then waived by Olympiacos in December 2009.[http://www.talkbasket.net/von-wafer-history-for-olympiacos-officially-2391 Talkbasket.net Von Wafer history for Olympiacos, officially.] Wafer shot 36.4% from the field and averaged 3.0 points per game and 1.3 rebounds per game in the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek A1 League]] with Olympiacos.[http://www.galanissportsdata.com/basketball/mena1/Season2009_10/a1teamrs.asp?t=02 Galanissportsdata.com OLYMPIACOS (Total Stats Regular Season After day 6).] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105041727/http://www.galanissportsdata.com/basketball/mena1/Season2009_10/a1teamrs.asp?t=02 |date=2010-01-05 }} In Euroleague play, he shot 50% from the field and averaged 7.7 points per game, 1.3 rebounds per game, and 1.0 assists per game.[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?clubcode=OLY&pcode=001924&seasoncode=e2009 Euroleague.net WAFER, VON.] ===Dallas Mavericks=== On February 24, 2010, Wafer signed a ten-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4666359/wafers-officially-a-maverick Wafer's officially a Maverick – Dallas Mavericks Blog – ESPN Dallas] He was not expected to crack the rotation during his tenure and although he was eligible to play six games,[https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=4940999 Dallas Mavericks sign Von Wafer to 10-day contract – ESPN Dallas] Wafer finished his contract with Dallas without playing a single minute.[https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4676024/report-cs-sign-von-wafer Report: C's sign Von Wafer – Boston Celtics Blog – ESPN Boston] ===Boston Celtics=== On July 3, 2010, Wafer signed a free agent deal with the [[Boston Celtics]].[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press080310-wafer.html Celtics sign Wafer] On October 29, 2010, he was involved in a locker-room altercation with new teammate [[Delonte West]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/10/29/boston-celtics-fight.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2 |title=Wafer, West brawl after Celtics practice |work=NBA.com |date=2010-10-29 |access-date=2010-12-29}} ===Vanoli-Braga Cremona=== In August 2011, during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], he signed a one-year contract with [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli-Braga Cremona]] in Italy.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/30155/vanoli_cremona_agreed_to_terms_with_von_wafer.html Vanoli Cremona agreed to terms with Von Wafer] ===Orlando Magic=== Wafer was traded to the Magic on December 12, 2011, along with [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen Davis]] for [[Brandon Bass]].{{cite web | title = Magic Acquire Glen Davis and Von Wafer | url = http://www.nba.com/magic/news_davis_121211.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2011-12-12 | access-date = 2011-12-13}} He was waived by the Magic at the end of the 2011–12 season.[https://web.archive.org/web/20151016145040/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-05-29/sports/os-magic-waive-von-wafer-0530-20120529_1_orlando-magic-von-wafer-magic-roster Orlando Magic waive Von Wafer] ===Move to CBA=== Wafer moved to China in 2012, signed a one-year contract with Xinjiang Flying Tigers worth $2 million. He played 34 games for Xinjiang, averaged 26.4 points with a shooting percentage of 55.4%. He also got 4.4 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.1 steals per game.{{cite web|last=HoopChina.com|title=CBA Statistics (In Chinese)|url=http://cba.hupu.com/players/weifu.html|access-date=21 October 2013|archive-date=October 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021220246/http://cba.hupu.com/players/weifu.html|url-status=dead}} In October 2013, he signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]], the team owned by his former teammate [[Yao Ming]] at the [[Houston Rockets|Rockets]].[http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/64822/von-wafer-signs-with-shanghai-sharks.html Von Wafer signs with Shanghai Sharks] In December 2013, he left the Sharks. ===Bakersfield Jam=== On January 10, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_acquires_von_wafer_2014_01_10.html Bakersfield Acquires Von Wafer] On January 28, 2014, he was waived by the Jam. ===Russia=== On February 3, 2014, he signed with [[BC Krasny Oktyabr]] for the rest of the 2013–2014 season.{{cite news|title=Von Wafer signs in Russia with Krasny Oktyabr Volgograd|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/cups/vtb-league/73194/von-wafer-signs-in-russia-with-krasny-oktyabr-volgograd.html|access-date=February 7, 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=February 3, 2014}} ===Delaware 87ers=== On November 26, 2016, Wafer returned to the United States, signing with the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|title=RELEASE: SEVENS ADD VON WAFER|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/release-sevens-add-von-wafer/|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2016|access-date=December 2, 2016|archive-date=December 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202175212/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/release-sevens-add-von-wafer/|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|first=Dakota|last=Schmidt|title=Von Wafer Signs With The Delaware 87ers. Can He Have One Last NBA Opportunity?|url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2016/11/26/13752800/von-wafer-nba-dleague-delaware-87ers|work=[[SBNation.com]]|date=November 26, 2016|access-date=November 29, 2016|archive-date=November 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161127130003/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2016/11/26/13752800/von-wafer-nba-dleague-delaware-87ers|url-status=dead}} ===Westchester Knicks=== On December 14, 2016, Wafer was traded to the [[Westchester Knicks]] in exchange for [[Devondrick Walker]].{{cite web|first=Katie|last=Hatch|title=WESTCHESTER KNICKS ACQUIRE VON WAFER|url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-von-wafer/|work=NBA.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}} ===Return to CBA=== On August 27, 2017, Wafer returned to China, signing with the [[Jilin Northeast Tigers]].{{cite web|title=Von Wafer signs with Northeast Tigers|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/245328/von-wafer-signs-with-northeast-tigers.html|website=Sportando|access-date=August 27, 2017|date=August 27, 2017}} == NBA career statistics == {{NBA player statistics legend}} === Regular season === {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2005}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2005–06 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
